title: Comparison Operators
body:
The six operators that take two values and produce a [[Boolean]]: `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`,
`!=`. They are what a [[Conditional]] tests.

```python
age >= 18        # True or False
name == "Evan"   # works on strings too, and compares contents
count != 0
```

**`==` compares, `=` assigns.** This is the single most common beginner error and it is worth
saying plainly: `x = 5` stores, `x == 5` asks. Python helps here in a way C does not, by making
`if x = 5:` a `SyntaxError` outright rather than a legal assignment that evaluates to 5 and is
always true. See [[Augmented Assignment]].

Comparisons work on [[String|strings]] by lexicographic order (`"apple" < "banana"`), which is
character-code order and therefore puts every uppercase letter before every lowercase one.
`"Zebra" < "apple"` is True, and that surprises people once each.

Python allows chaining, which most languages do not: `0 <= x <= 10` means what it looks like.

Combine them with [[Logical Operators]].
